title: Guitar Practice Tracker — Tuner and Audio Input
description: Setting up your audio interface or microphone in Guitar Practice, and using the tuner for guitar or bass in standard, drop and open tunings, or a custom tuning.

scenes.text: This video covers your audio input, and the tuner.
Set up your input once, in Settings. Pick your audio interface or microphone. If your interface has two inputs, pick the one your guitar is plugged into.
Press Test input and play. The level bar should pass the line, which is the noise gate. Raise the input boost if it doesn't. The A four reference is normally four hundred and forty hertz.
The tuner listens as soon as you open its tab, and stops when you leave. Pluck a string. It shows the note, how many cents you're off, and lights the string it thinks you're tuning.
When the needle is in the middle and the note turns green, the string is in tune.

Under Tuning, pick guitar or bass, the number of strings, and a tuning. There are standard, drop, open, and lowered tunings for six, seven, and eight string guitars, and four, five, and six string basses.
Or set each string yourself. The tuner then follows your custom tuning.
